questions.stem: With reference to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls conducted by the Election Commission of India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls is conducted by the Election Commission of India under powers derived from the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

Under SIR guidelines, a Booth Level Officer may mark an elector's name for the Absent/Shifted/Dead/Duplicate (ASDD) category based on local inquiry, even if the elector does not return the enumeration form.
A person whose name is deleted from the draft electoral roll during SIR has no legal remedy and must wait for the next roll revision cycle to be re-included.
questions.explanation: Preparation and revision of electoral rolls is governed by the Representation of the People Act, 1950 (Sections 21-23), so statement 1 is correct. The article confirms BLOs identify a 'probable cause' such as ASDD from neighbour inquiry when forms are not returned, making statement 2 correct. Statement 3 is wrong because EC guidelines explicitly allow an aggrieved elector to file a claim/objection against deletion during the draft-roll stage itself, not just at the next cycle.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Raghav Chadha out of Punjab draft roll: How does SIR delete a name, and how can it be restored
questions.pyqLink: Tests EC's roll-revision powers under RPA 1950 and safeguards against wrongful deletion; similar in spirit to UPSC 2017 questions on Election Commission's constitutional/statutory functions.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding coal supply arrangements for India's thermal power sector. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The Central Electricity Authority's plant-specific coal-stocking norms took effect in December 2021.
Under the revised SHAKTI policy, Window I coal linkages are allotted to central and state government generating utilities at notified prices, while Window II is for procurement through auctions.
The Ministries of Coal, Power and Railways coordinate to monitor coal supplies and their movement to power plants.
Fuel Supply Agreements (FSAs) are arrangements exclusively between state governments and coal-importing private companies.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the CEA framework became effective from December 6, 2021. Statement 2 is correct as per the article's description of Window I (notified prices for public utilities) and Window II (auction, including for imported-coal-based plants). Statement 3 is correct — the article confirms inter-ministerial coordination. Statement 4 is wrong: FSAs are signed between coal companies (like Coal India) and consumers generally, not 'exclusively' between state governments and coal-importing private firms.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Coal stock management emerges as key challenge for thermal power producers
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional detail on coal-linkage policy (SHAKTI) and CEA norms, similar to UPSC's recurring questions on energy-sector regulatory bodies and policies.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about Mizoram, seen recently in the news over a rail-link disruption. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: Mizoram's rail connectivity to the rest of India runs through a line passing via Assam's Barak Valley.
The recent disruption to this rail link was caused by a landslide triggered by an earthquake.
Rail infrastructure in Mizoram falls under the jurisdiction of the Northeast Frontier Railway, headquartered at Guwahati.
Mizoram shares an international border with Myanmar but not with Bangladesh.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the affected Katakhal-Bairabi section links Assam (Jamira) to Mizoram (Bairabi) through the Barak Valley. Statement 2 is wrong — the article attributes the disruption to soil erosion from heavy rainfall, not an earthquake. Statement 3 is correct — the NFR's CPRO is quoted, and NFR is headquartered at Maligaon, Guwahati. Statement 4 is wrong — Mizoram borders both Myanmar and Bangladesh internationally.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Heavy rain disrupts train services to Mizoram, repair work underway
questions.pyqLink: Tests physical/political geography of a Northeastern state and railway zone jurisdiction, in the style of UPSC's state-boundary and infrastructure-zone questions.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs relating to the integration of princely states into independent India, in the context of a long-running Vadodara land dispute involving the erstwhile royal family. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Instrument of Accession
Legal document by which a princely ruler acceded their state to the Indian Union
Privy Purse
Hereditary payment to former rulers, abolished by the 26th Constitutional Amendment (1971)
Doctrine of Lapse
Policy under which Baroda State was annexed by the British in 1802 for want of a natural heir
Sanad
Royal charter or deed historically issued by a ruling authority granting land, title, or privilege
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correctly matched with their standard constitutional/historical meanings. Pair 3 is wrong: the Doctrine of Lapse was Lord Dalhousie's 19th-century policy (1848-56) for annexing states lacking a natural male heir, but Baroda was never annexed under it — it continued as a princely state under the Gaekwad dynasty until its 1949 accession to India.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: How a land dispute involving Vadodara's royal family has lasted over 50 years — and counting
questions.pyqLink: Tests concepts around princely-state integration (Instrument of Accession, Privy Purse, Doctrine of Lapse), a recurring UPSC theme, e.g. UPSC 2018 question on Doctrine of Lapse and annexations.

questions.stem: With reference to frontier artificial intelligence systems such as OpenAI's newly released model, the term 'agentic AI' is best described as which one of the following?
options: An AI model restricted to answering natural-language prompts without any ability to interact with external software or interfaces
An AI system capable of autonomously performing multi-step tasks — such as operating browsers, filling forms, or editing documents — to achieve a goal with minimal step-by-step human instruction
An AI model whose training data is restricted exclusively to content generated by other AI systems
An AI system that can only be accessed through an Application Programming Interface (API) and never through a conversational chat interface
questions.explanation: The article describes the new model as one built for 'end-to-end work' — operating computers/browsers, filling forms, updating records and troubleshooting — which is the defining feature of agentic AI: autonomous, multi-step task execution rather than single-turn prompt response. The other options describe unrelated or opposite characteristics (passive chatbots, synthetic-data-only training, or API-only access) that do not capture agency.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: OpenAI's new Astra model can code better. But here's why its cybersecurity skills matter as much
questions.pyqLink: Tests conceptual understanding of 'agentic AI' versus conventional generative AI, an emerging static concept UPSC has begun probing via terms like 'Merchant Discount Rate' style best-describes questions (UPSC 2019).

questions.stem:
Consider the following two statements in the context of Kenya's dispute with Tata Chemicals over its Magadi soda ash plant.
Statement-I: The dispute reflects a concern common to several resource-rich developing countries about long-term resource-extraction contracts with foreign firms yielding insufficient local industrial development.
Statement-II: Bilateral Investment Treaties (BITs) between India and African nations guarantee automatic renewal of all mining and mineral-extraction concessions held by Indian companies.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct — the Kenyan President's core grievance (long tenure, extraction of minerals, insufficient local factories/investment in Kajiado) is a recurring theme in host-country disputes with foreign resource firms globally. Statement-II is incorrect — BITs typically provide protections such as fair and equitable treatment or safeguards against expropriation, but they do not guarantee 'automatic renewal' of any specific mining or extraction concession, which remains subject to the host country's domestic contract/licensing law.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Kenyan President vs Tata Chemicals: Why Kenya wants Tata firm’s operations halted
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static concept of Bilateral Investment Treaties and host-state regulatory sovereignty over natural resources, relevant to India's economic diplomacy with Africa.

questions.stem: With reference to Himalayan glacial hazards and international climate negotiations, in the context of the recent Nepal-Tibet border flash flood, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) occurs when a moraine or ice dam holding back a glacial lake fails suddenly, releasing a large volume of water downstream.

The principle of 'Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities' (CBDR-RC), enshrined in the UNFCCC, holds that all countries bear identical emission-reduction obligations regardless of their historical contribution to global emissions.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly defines a GLOF, the phenomenon underlying the glacier-collapse-triggered flash flood referenced in the article. Statement 2 is incorrect because CBDR-RC, as recognised under the UNFCCC, explicitly differentiates obligations based on historical responsibility and respective capability — it does not impose 'identical' obligations on all countries, which is the opposite of what India's MEA invoked in the article.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: 'Climate change a common challenge': India on Nepal's 'justice' demand
questions.pyqLink: Tests GLOF mechanics and the CBDR-RC principle under UNFCCC, both recurring static concepts behind climate-news triggers (cf. UPSC questions on Rio Conventions and climate equity principles).

questions.stem: With reference to government bonds, consider the following statements. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
statements: Statement-I: A sell-off in government bonds is generally accompanied by a rise in bond yields.
Statement-II: The price of a bond and its yield are inversely related, so a fall in bond prices raises the effective yield to a new buyer.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Bond price and yield move inversely because a bond's coupon is fixed; when investors sell, prices fall, and the fixed coupon then represents a higher percentage return (yield) on the lower price. This inverse relationship is precisely why a sell-off raises yields, so Statement-II correctly explains Statement-I.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: How the global bond sell-off could affect India | Explained
questions.pyqLink: Tests the bond price-yield relationship, a recurring static concept behind UPSC's monetary policy and G-Sec questions (cf. UPSC 2021 RBI expansionary policy question).

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of institutions involved in estimating India's manufacturing sector output and their functions. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: National Statistical Office (NSO)
Compiles the National Accounts Statistics, including manufacturing GVA, for the country
Annual Survey of Industries (ASI)
Covers production accounts of the registered/organised factory sector
Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE)
Covers household and informal manufacturing units outside the factory sector
Reserve Bank of India
Conducts the Annual Survey of Industries
questions.explanation: NSO compiles the NAS, ASI covers the registered/organised factory sector, and ASUSE covers unincorporated/informal units — all correctly matched. The fourth pair is wrong: the ASI is conducted by the NSO/MoSPI, not the RBI, which has no role in industrial surveys.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: The gap in manufacturing sector GVA
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional ownership of national statistical surveys, a recurring 'who publishes what' static theme (cf. UPSC questions on NSO, ASI and National Accounts Statistics).

questions.stem: With reference to Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), which operates the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: RINL functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Steel.
RINL holds Maharatna status among Central Public Sector Enterprises.
questions.explanation: RINL, the corporate entity running the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, is administered under the Ministry of Steel, making Statement 1 correct. However, RINL is classified as a Miniratna Category-I CPSE, not a Maharatna, so Statement 2 is incorrect.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Vizag MP Sribharat hopeful of turnaround in VSP fortune
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Maharatna/Navratna/Miniratna CPSE classification scheme, a recurring institutional-detail theme in governance questions.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety (CMRS), which recently cleared new trainsets for the Bengaluru Metro. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: CMRS grants safety clearance before new rolling stock is inducted into commercial service on metro networks.
CMRS functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, and not the Ministry of Railways.
CMRS's safety certification function applies only to metro railways, while the Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS) organisation certifies the broader Indian Railways network.
CMRS derives its statutory powers from the Railways Act, 1989.
questions.explanation: The first three statements are correct: CMRS clears new rolling stock, is kept under the Ministry of Civil Aviation for independence from the Railway Board, and its jurisdiction is limited to metro systems. The fourth is wrong — CMRS derives its powers from the Metro Railways (Operation and Maintenance) Act, 2002, not the Railways Act, 1989, which governs the broad-gauge network.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: BMRCL gets safety nod to induct new six-car trains on Purple, Green Lines
questions.pyqLink: Tests statutory vs administrative control of railway safety bodies, in the Commission's favoured 'which ministry, which Act' institutional-detail style.

questions.stem: With reference to India's satellite launch vehicles, consider the following statements about the recent GSLV-F17 launch of EOS-05. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: GSLV-F17 placed EOS-05 into a Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit, from which the satellite will use onboard propulsion to reach its final orbit.
A satellite placed in geosynchronous orbit necessarily appears stationary relative to a point on the Earth's surface.
The GSLV rocket uses an indigenously developed cryogenic upper stage, unlike the PSLV, which does not use a cryogenic stage.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — Sub-GTO insertion followed by onboard propulsion to reach final orbit is standard GSLV practice. Statement 3 is correct — GSLV uses an indigenous cryogenic upper stage while PSLV does not. Statement 2 is wrong: only a geostationary orbit (zero inclination, circular, equatorial) appears stationary; a geosynchronous orbit with inclination produces an apparent north-south drift.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: ISRO successfully launches Earth observation satellite EOS-05
questions.pyqLink: Tests the geosynchronous vs geostationary distinction and GSLV vs PSLV propulsion, a recurring space-technology static theme.

questions.stem: With reference to map projections, and in the context of the UN resolution favouring the Equal Earth projection over the Mercator projection, which one of the following best explains why the Mercator projection makes Greenland appear roughly the same size as Africa?
options: The Mercator projection is an equal-area projection that preserves true relative size everywhere at the cost of shape.
The Mercator projection is a conformal cylindrical projection that preserves angles and shapes for navigation but progressively inflates the area of landmasses farther from the equator.
The Mercator projection is centred on the Prime Meridian, which distorts longitudinal distances near the poles.
The Mercator projection is an azimuthal projection that distorts distances only along great-circle routes.
questions.explanation: The Mercator projection is a conformal cylindrical projection, valued for preserving angles/shapes for navigation, but this comes at the cost of increasingly exaggerating the area of regions away from the equator (like Greenland) relative to equatorial regions (like Africa). It is not equal-area (option A), its distortion is latitude-driven, not centred on a meridian (option C), and it is cylindrical, not azimuthal (option D).
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: U.N. approves resolution in support of map that shows Africa’s true size
questions.pyqLink: Tests properties of map projections (conformal/equal-area/azimuthal), a standard static geography syllabus topic.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding resolutions of the United Nations, in the context of the recent UN General Assembly resolution on map projections. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: A UN General Assembly resolution is legally binding on all UN member states.
Resolutions of the UN Security Council adopted under Chapter VII of the UN Charter are binding on member states.
Each member state in the UN General Assembly has one vote, regardless of its population or economic size.
A permanent member of the UN Security Council can veto a resolution being voted upon in the General Assembly.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Chapter VII Security Council resolutions are binding, and the General Assembly follows one-state-one-vote. Statement 1 is wrong — General Assembly resolutions are generally recommendatory, not binding, which is why the map resolution itself was explicitly described as not legally binding. Statement 4 is wrong — the veto power of permanent members applies only within the Security Council, not in General Assembly voting.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: U.N. approves resolution in support of map that shows Africa’s true size
questions.pyqLink: Tests the binding/non-binding distinction between UNGA and UNSC resolutions and the veto mechanism, a recurring UN-institutional static theme.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding Myristica swamps, a rare ecosystem found in the Western Ghats:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Myristica swamps are freshwater swamp forests found in a restricted patch of the Western Ghats.
Plants in these swamps exhibit adaptations such as pneumatophores and stilt roots to survive waterlogged conditions.
Like Myristica swamps, mangrove forests are also freshwater ecosystems.
Freshwater swamp forests occupy more than one-tenth of the Earth's land surface.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Myristica swamps are a rare freshwater swamp ecosystem in Kerala's Western Ghats with plants adapted via pneumatophores and stilt roots. Statement 3 is wrong because mangroves occur in brackish/saltwater habitats, not freshwater, unlike Myristica swamps. Statement 4 is wrong because freshwater swamp forests occupy no more than 2.1% of the Earth's surface, not over 10%.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Rare freshwater swamps in the Western Ghats are on the cusp of extinction
questions.pyqLink: Tests static concept of wetland/swamp ecosystem classification, similar to UPSC questions on mangroves vs. other wetland types (e.g., 2015 mangrove characteristics question)

questions.stem: With reference to Hawking radiation and black holes, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Hawking radiation causes black holes to lose mass over time, with smaller black holes evaporating faster than larger ones.
The Hawking temperature of a black hole is directly proportional to its mass.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Hawking radiation causes black holes to lose mass, and smaller black holes evaporate faster, as noted in the study on dark-matter-fed black holes inside stars. Statement 2 is incorrect: a black hole's Hawking temperature is inversely proportional to its mass, meaning smaller black holes are hotter and evaporate quicker, not the reverse.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Dark matter could keep tiny black holes alive inside stars: study
questions.pyqLink: Tests static astrophysics concept of black hole thermodynamics/Hawking radiation, an emerging Sci-Tech theme in recent prelims papers

questions.stem: With reference to India's foreign exchange reserves, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: India's forex reserves comprise Foreign Currency Assets, gold, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), and India's reserve position with the IMF.
Foreign Currency Assets held in India's forex reserves are denominated and held only in US dollars.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct and matches the RBI's standard four-component classification of forex reserves confirmed in the weekly data release. Statement 2 is incorrect because Foreign Currency Assets are held in multiple currencies such as the euro, pound and yen, with their dollar value reflecting appreciation or depreciation of these non-US currencies, not held exclusively in dollars.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the El Nino phenomenon:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: El Nino refers to the warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean.
El Nino events are directly caused by anthropogenic climate change.
The World Meteorological Organization is the UN specialized agency responsible for monitoring and forecasting El Nino conditions.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: El Nino is the warming of the central-eastern equatorial Pacific, and the WMO, the UN's climate and weather agency, monitors and forecasts it. Statement 2 is incorrect because El Nino is explicitly described as a naturally occurring phenomenon not caused by climate change, though climate change can amplify its impacts.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of bodies involved in air quality and environmental regulation and their descriptions:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM)
A statutory body constituted under an Act of Parliament to coordinate air pollution management in Delhi-NCR
National Green Tribunal (NGT)
A statutory body established under a dedicated Act for effective and speedy disposal of environment-related cases
Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)
A constitutional body responsible for setting national ambient air quality standards
Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)
An executive body under the Department of Space that provides satellite-based data used for tracking farm fires
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correctly matched: CAQM was constituted under the CAQM Act, 2021; NGT was set up under the NGT Act, 2010; and ISRO, under the Department of Space, supplies satellite fire-count data referenced in CAQM's stubble-burning estimation discussions. Pair 3 is incorrect because CPCB is a statutory body under the Water Act, 1974 and Air Act, 1981, not a constitutional body.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: CAQM in talks with Punjab, Haryana to improve stubble burning estimation protocol
questions.pyqLink: Tests static concept of statutory vs constitutional vs executive bodies in environmental governance, similar to UPSC questions distinguishing NGT/CPCB/NITI Aayog status

questions.stem: The recent public pressure by the US President on the Federal Reserve Chair to cut interest rates has renewed debate on 'central bank independence'. Which one of the following best describes this concept?
options: The central bank's freedom to determine monetary policy instruments, such as interest rates, without direct political interference, while remaining accountable to the legislature for its mandate
A constitutional provision empowering the central bank to override fiscal policy decisions taken by the elected government
The central bank's exemption from all forms of government audit and legislative oversight
The practice of central banks fixing exchange rates independent of movements in the foreign exchange market
questions.explanation: Central bank independence means the central bank can operationally decide monetary policy tools free of day-to-day political pressure, while still being accountable to the legislature for outcomes like inflation control, illustrated by the Fed resisting presidential pressure to cut rates. Option B wrongly conflates monetary independence with overriding fiscal policy; option C is wrong as central banks remain subject to audit and oversight; option D wrongly describes an exchange-rate regime, not policy independence.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: 'Lower interest rates or...,' Trump turns up heat on hand-picked Fed chair Kevin Warsh, threatens trade shutdown
questions.pyqLink: Tests static concept of central bank autonomy and monetary policy governance, relevant to RBI Act provisions and similar to UPSC's recurring monetary policy questions
